sessions.date: 2026-10-21 session 56 (#853, #856, #857 merged: the ai-review drift reading stopped measuring index state)
items: #855 landed #853. The drift check compared whole `git status --porcelain` lines, status prefix included, and the restore step writes the index twice per path (`git rm`, then `git checkout` from the base). So the baseline recorded a staged `M ` and anything that unstaged before the second reading turned the same path into ` M` — same file, same bytes, one space moved, reported as something the reviewer did. PR #815 was the live reproduction. AI_REVIEW_TREE_READER is now one binding interpolated into both steps, emitting `<content-hash|absent> <path>`: the prefix carried exactly one thing the comparison needed (modification against deletion against untracked-add) and content carries it better.

The issue asked for `git reset` after the checkout. Measured as mutation row M3, that is neither necessary nor sufficient, and the row is the whole argument: it DOES cure the reported symptom — both SC-1 cases green — and it also reds "an edit to a RESTORED path is refused and names it", which the defective tree does NOT red. Every restored path is already dirty in the baseline, and porcelain reports that a path differs from the index, never how; today's refusal was a by-product of the staged/unstaged distinction, which is the thing the reset removes. So the repair that makes #815 pass is the repair that stops catching a reviewer editing an agent-rules file. One mutation, a fix in one direction and a regression in the other.

M7 came back 0 and that was a finding about the change rather than about the cases: the reader's rename/copy branch had no fixture, so making it unreachable changed nothing observable. The branch was not deleted — a rename line puts two paths in one field, so the file reads `absent` and the two readings then agree on `absent` whatever the reviewer does to the destination — a case was added instead, the row became 1, the baseline moved 94 to 95, and every other row was re-measured against it rather than carried over.

#858 landed #856, three ways past the drift check that measuring content does not reach. `escape_annotation` was declared inside buildDriftScript and used at four of eleven annotation sites that interpolate a shell value; the other seven put the value straight into `::error title=...::`, and GitHub decodes `%0A` in an annotation body. Demonstrated live before the repair, not argued. Mixed is worse than neither: a reader asking "is this escaped" finds the helper and stops, and the yes was true of four lines. The rule now enforced is mechanical rather than a reachability judgement — three of the seven were generator-controlled, escaping them costs nothing, and the alternative asks every future editor to redo the analysis correctly.

The other two: both readings honour `.gitignore`, which was not in the restored set, so a head adding `.claude/**` removed a reviewer-created file from the baseline AND the after-reading, and a file in neither is in no difference. And `git hash-object` applied the repository's own text/eol conversion, so two different working-tree blobs hashed identically — under `* text eol=lf`, CRLF and LF both hash 587be6b4, and `--no-filters` gives db127bf6 and 587be6b4.

A correction to #856's AC-9 worth keeping: it asks for `.gitattributes` in the restored set and says both repairs are required. For `.gitignore` that is right and the battery shows it. For `.gitattributes` no reachable attack could be produced — row N5 reddened only an assertion that the name appears in the list, which restates the change, and the obvious attack does not work: measured, a head `.gitattributes` declaring `* text eol=lf` does not hide a CRLF-for-LF worktree edit from `git status`, which still reports ` M`. `--no-filters` is what closes that finding. The entry stays because `.gitattributes` configures how git reads the tree, but its case now runs the restore and reads the tree, and the weaker claim is labelled as weaker rather than dressed up.

#859 landed #857. lib/scaffold/ai-review-step.ts is a generator and .github/workflows/ai-review.yml is its committed output, and nothing compared the two — so both earlier phases could have landed correct in CI and absent from the generator, with the next scaffold run silently reverting them. The case regenerates into a scratch directory from this repo's own config and compares bytes, rather than checking step containment: two per-step containment cases already existed and each passes over every line it does not name.

The second half is the measurement's own integrity. A suite whose count stayed flat while its subject changed is indistinguishable from one whose disagreeing cases were rewritten to agree with the new code. .claude/ai-review-surface-ratchet.json holds the 248 ai-review case titles as they stood at bc56a7c2; 272 now, 0 of the 248 missing, 24 added. The baseline is a committed file and not a `git show` of that commit because CI checks out shallow, and a reading that could not be taken is not a reading that passed. The census excludes its own file, and the exclusion is asserted rather than written, because removing it changes no verdict except the one case that looks for it.

FIVE security rounds on one parse function, every round finding a real differential between the guard and what the gh binary actually does. Checked against the binary instead of reasoning about it: the LAST --repo wins, -R is a real alias, GH_REPO is honoured. Round 3's bypass paired the FIRST issue number with the LAST repo. Round 4's was the detector requiring digits straight after `close`, so `gh issue close --repo a/b 23` matched nothing and the guard stepped aside entirely — a miss, not a wrong answer. An over-matching detector costs a refusal; an under-matching one is silent, so detection is now deliberately loose and the number is read afterwards, refusing when several numbers are candidates. Round 5 was not attempted: filed as #144, because the class is unwinnable from a regex over a command string and five rounds is well past Three Strikes.

CI caught a real bug in my own security fix. I had restricted GITHUB_API_URL to loopback; GitHub Actions sets GITHUB_API_URL=https://api.github.com on every run, so the whole suite failed in CI while passing locally where the variable is unset. Per 'remove the difference, not the failures' the fix went in the CODE, not the tests: an exact-hostname allowlist of {api.github.com, github.com, loopback}. api.github.com.evil.com and a loopback name in the userinfo are both still refused.

39 mutations across the branch, 0 survivors — but FIVE of them survived first time, and each survivor exposed a vacuous test of mine. The empty-token case did not exercise the trim at all ('' is falsy, so it threw on the truthiness check either way); the multi-close count was shielded by the separator check; every command-substitution case was shielded by the literal-slug check; and the comment-template rules had NO coverage whatsoever — mutations neutering the entire validator ran green against 26 existing guard tests. 'Shielded mutation' is the name for this: the mutation survives because a DIFFERENT defence catches the test case, so the test proves nothing about the line it appears to cover.

The symlink guard is a COST guard: removing it was 0 red of 92, and SC-1877 now feeds a dirent that DISAGREES with the filesystem, the only shape in which a saved syscall is visible to a test.

#557 landed #531. Three gate checks built their changed-file list with ${scopeSha}..HEAD. Two dots compares two commits directly, so a scope sha that is not an ancestor of HEAD drags in the other side of the fork: on run wf_e230fddc-a71 the branch touched 3 files, the gate saw 78 and refused over a Dockerfile and seven .tsx files the branch has never contained. The sha was wrong a second, independent way — writeGateResult recorded gitSha(projectRoot) while the run shipped a worktree — and either half alone still mis-attributes. The commit security review found a third: git C-quotes any non-ASCII path, so src/café.tsx leaves every downstream filename regex as a quoted string and walks past quinn-on-ui-change. Same defect through the encoding; -z is the fix.

#558 landed #549. bunx rungate scaffold . could not run on this repo: the audit clone copied the WHOLE tree and applied REHEARSAL_EXCLUDES afterwards — 737 MB across 104 worktrees copied and then handed to a delete that died with EFAULT. The exclude list was right; the ORDERING defeated it. Absence cannot witness the fix, because the excluded path is absent under both orderings; the witnesses are an excluded directory that cannot be READ and the list of cp invocations through an injected runner.

#549's stated diagnosis was incomplete and the correction is half the fix. The EFAULT is not the size: cp -Rc is a clonefile and a clonefile carries BSD file flags, so the clone held the uchg files this repo sets on gates/prompts/*.md and rm answered Operation not permitted. Three places deleted a tree the module made and two were bare rmSync; all three go through one removeTree now — clear flags, restore owner rwX, delete, fall back to /bin/rm -rf — and a cleanup failure is a sentence the caller prints rather than a throw that discards the report it already produced.

It shipped green twice and came back red on Linux CI both times, and the lesson is about the FIXTURE, not the code. GNU cp -R creates its destination with the source's mode; macOS's creates it from the umask and fails before chmodding. So the leftover an unreadable source produces differs by platform, and every mutation measured its prediction exactly on a tree that crashed. The control's unreadable directory is now an ancestor of an exclude, which the WALK creates and chmods: the shape is built by the test rather than by cp. When a fixture's shape is produced by a tool rather than by the test, the test is measuring that tool's behaviour on the machine it ran on.

#559 landed #382 and #552 — two scaffold warnings that had been firing on rungate itself for weeks. #382 had been closed on 2026-10-14 without being fixed, five minutes after a cross-reference from #383 that never touched either check; found by reproducing the warnings live rather than trusting the tracker, and reopened with evidence. `lib/spec-listing.ts` is now the one binding for what counts as a spec and what counts as a LISTING of one. A mutation row came back 1 where 2 was predicted, and the cause is the distinction the module now makes: a whole-document `includes` counted a prose MENTION of `specs/SPEC-TEMPLATE.md` in `.claude/rules/checks-must-be-able-to-fail.md` as a routing-table entry. A mention is not a listing. `updateSpecsTable` was deleted outright — it had been a silent no-op.

#560 landed #501 — a consumer whose only code was `workflows/*.ts` got two unsatisfiable refusals, CONFIG-1 and CONFIG-2 each declining the directory it thought the other had. CONFIG-2's module scan was `.js`-only and non-recursive; it is now `SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` and recursive, and CONFIG-1 declines `workflows/` by name with a sentence saying who does measure it. Deliberately a `CONFIG_1_DECLINES` set and not `measuredElsewhere`: `test/` is a policy exclusion nobody measures, so it must still refuse, which is #500's case. Widening it to `measuredElsewhere` is 4 red where 1 was predicted, and the three extras are exactly those.

#561 addressed #506 partially — `walkSources` filtered on `/\.(ts|js)$/` while the evidence walk beside it counted seven extensions, so a project whose only code is `lib/app.tsx` holding a live config read reported `filesScanned: 0` and a refusal whose sentence is false about the file it names. #506 stays OPEN and assigned: its remaining case, `docs/assets/search.js`, is a scope decision about what CONFIG-1 is responsible for, and the measured analysis of all four options is posted on the issue. #562 landed #488 — the generated CI workflow hardcoded `bun test` with `harness` in scope, four lines below three reads of `harness?.ci?.*`. Four sites resolved one question four ways, so a project declaring `dev.testCmd` got briefs, an AGENTS.md row and a ship workflow with their command and a CI workflow with a different one. `lib/test-command.ts` is the one ladder. The wiring then broke the config REPAIR step, which runs over the malformed configs it exists to repair and died on the throwing loader; that site calls `inferredTestCommand`, the same ladder without the config rung — which it needed anyway, since the value it computes is what gets written INTO `dev.testCmd`. Two mutation rows missed low by the same case, and it was not a collapsed pair: a template test handed a hand-built scan object, downstream of the binding rather than part of it.

#563 landed #503 — the SC id allocator read `specs/` in whichever working tree it ran in, and this machine has 110 worktrees of the repository. Two sessions took the same block on 2026-10-16 and both guards were green. `lib/sc-id-cross-tree.ts` reads sibling worktrees (which catches an id typed and not yet committed) and every local and remote-tracking ref (which catches one committed on a branch whose worktree is gone); `allocateScNumber` is where all three widths compose. Deliberately NOT a refusal on cross-tree duplicates: measured, 30 ids are declared in more than one spec file across those 110 trees, every one an anti-criterion or a collision resolved months ago and fossilised in a stale tree.

#564 landed #497 — #439 allowed a `contextDocs` path outside the project root on the premise that the config is written by the operator whose session the agent runs in. True of a project they scaffolded, false of one they cloned, where the config is a checked-in file somebody else wrote. External paths are refused now and NAMED in the brief, which keeps #439's actual property; trust comes from `RUNGATE_TRUSTED_DOC_ROOTS` in the environment, because an allowlist inside the config it is allowing is not one. The comparison moved to the real path — `ln -s ~/.ssh docs` resolved under the root and read as internal — and the AC `contextFiles` door goes through the same classifier, since a control on one of two doors is what #439 itself said the old filter was.

#565 landed #471 — and the shape it was filed as does not catch the case that filed it. `git check-ignore --no-index node_modules` exits 1 against a tracked symlink, and asking about a path below the link is `fatal: beyond a symbolic link`, so a detector built on `ls-files` and `check-ignore` agreeing is narrower than the thing it was written to detect. Two findings instead: the filed contradiction, and a tracked symlink whose target is absolute — which needs no ignore rule, because no `.gitignore` edit could make a committed host path right. 913 tracked paths, 0 contradictions, 0 tracked symlinks, so no ratchet. The eighth mutation came from security review rather than the battery: a failing `cat-file` left the target null and the finding silently absent, making a broken read the cheapest way to clear the check.

#566 landed #510 — DIR-L29 charged a reviewer's /tmp probe at the same rate as this repository's 400-second suite, so sec-500 reached 8 of 8 running mutation probes on `git archive` exports without ever running the real suite, and reported two findings as unmeasured because of it. The more carefully someone reviewed, the less they were allowed to measure. `runScope` compares the shared git directory rather than a path, so all 110 worktrees are charged and a tree that is not this repository is not. It exempts the BUDGET and never the slot: the budget is a rate and the slot is simultaneity, `TestSuiteRelease` frees a slot on a predicate with no notion of scope, and `cd /tmp` must not be a way past the cap. One mutation row measured 0 and the 0 was the MUTANT — it tested the prefix of the git common dir, which for a worktree under tmp is the main repository's .git.

#567 landed #553 — two peer security reviews arrived measured against trees their branches had already moved past, and neither report said which tree. The receiving rule worked; the sending side had nothing. `lib/report-provenance.ts` imports `reviewIsCurrent` rather than repeating it, prefers `origin/<branch>` because that is what the reader can fetch, fetches nothing, and reports UNMEASURED for a detached HEAD or an unresolvable ref. One predicted-0 row stayed a hole until it was closed: the reading can be perfect while the three lines that actually travel omit the tip, which is the omission the issue is about.

#571 landed #507 — the scaffold's owned-file writer already refused a symlink; what shipped with the fix was one case driving `seedSuccessDoc`, which is create-only, while every other owned file is regenerate or provenance. A refusal measured on one strategy and described as belonging to all of them is a check narrower than its description. SC-1949 measures a dangling link and a live link to a file outside the project on a regenerate file, plus a real file as the positive control: 3 red and 3 red over 151 tests, where the first row was 1 before it existed. Two of my own defects fixed in passing. The id collided with a peer's unmerged block of nineteen, which the cross-tree allocator from #503 is the only reason anyone saw; and the collision then broke #503's own fixture, which planted its probe above this tree's spec registry rather than above the whole namespace. `nextSCNumber` is max+1, so the case witnesses the feature only while the probe IS the maximum — and there is a one-id window where it goes green having witnessed nothing. The margin was set by another session, in another worktree, at an unknown time: no mutation count finds that, which is why it is now a shape in checks-must-be-able-to-fail.md rather than a note in a PR.

Filed #570 and closed it the same hour as a duplicate of #508, which was a day old and said it better. The measurement was worth keeping and is now a comment there: HYGIENE-6's doc walk times at 4169, 4521 and 3969 ms against bun's 5000 ms default, on an idle machine with a warm cache, and its per-document `readFileSync` is unguarded, so a doc that moves mid-scan abandons the rest and the `expect(true).toBe(true)` below reports the partial scan as a pass. Search the open issues before filing; a duplicate costs a reader more than it cost me.

#575 landed #568 — specs/bootstrap-data-flow makes exactly one promise about user content, that the Hard Constraints section of AGENTS.md survives regeneration, and nothing implemented it: the scaffold built the file from a template and called writeFileSync. One run on a consumer removed 37 constraint lines and reported REGENERATED, exit 0. AGENTS.md turned out to be the only rewritten file in the tree with no declared strategy and no route through `decideOwnedWrite`, which is #208's whole point; it is `section-preserving` now, a fifth strategy rather than a special case at the call site, because a strategy implemented at a call site is how this one got lost. Routing it through the writer also closed a hole in #507 — a bare writeFileSync FOLLOWS a symlink, so the one file every consumer has was the one the refusal could not reach. The unit is the SECTION and not the marker pair: on the consumer that lost them, 8 lines were between the markers and 29 were hand-written after, so a marker-anchored fix would have rescued what a machine can regenerate and dropped what only a human holds. Five mutations, 2/2/3/1/1 over 134 tests. The golden fixture carries constraints now, which immediately turned SC-139 red — its 200-word cap is on the prose rungate writes, and counting a consumer's constraints against it means the cheapest way to pass is to delete constraints.

#577 landed #574 — sync-sc-status credited a criterion whose only test was a `test.todo`, which is the one test guaranteed never to fail. 64 ids named inside a todo, 53 with no other declaring mention, 37 ticked, and 19 more about to flip from another session's in-flight spec whose test file says in a comment four lines from the top that none of it is covered. The incentive was backwards the way #510's was: recording unfinished criteria honestly scored better than leaving them unmentioned. Two of the nineteen were credited by the sentence `(SC-1930..SC-1948) are NOT covered here` — a parenthetical of ids reads as an attribution, so the comment saying the criteria were not covered was the evidence that they were. A range is not an attribution and the scanner only sees ids literally written, so a range of nineteen credits its two endpoints and not the seventeen between: a form that credits 2 of the 19 ids it names is not measuring anything. 40 ticks removed, 2 restored by the conformity engine (a second legitimate credit path, which is why the live-tree ratchet asks for SOME measurement rather than a test file), two ratchets banked 39->35 and 100->66.

#578 landed #572 — PROJECT-STATE.md, the file AGENTS.md tells the next session to read first, rendered `[...sessions].reverse().slice(0, 3)`: the last three entries of the array, correct only while the array is in append order and nothing enforced that. Session 48 was written to sessions[0], so the whole of 2026-10-17 was invisible in the handoff all day while the script reported success on every run. Second instance in the same function — the first was slice(0,3) rendering the three OLDEST, fixed with .reverse(), which repaired the symptom and left the defect. By date now, so position stops mattering. Undated entries are RANKED below dated ones rather than dropped, because excluding them empties the handoff of any project whose dates are free-form, which is worse than the bug.

Four issues filed from inside other work and one of them closed as a duplicate within the hour: #570 (HYGIENE-6, already #508's part 1 — the measurement went to #508 as a comment and the issue closed; search the tracker before filing), #572, #574 and #579. #579 is that specs/PROJECT-STATE.md, which specs-routing.md calls the governing spec for project-state management, is a rendered snapshot from 2026-09-22 with spec frontmatter on top and zero criteria in it.

sessions.date: 2026-10-22 session 57 (eight merges closing out the ai-review adjudication and the refusal contract for failure intake; an npm partial outage masked three real failures)
items: #1115 landed #1110, and it is the consequential one of the eight. `buildReviewRunScript` wrote `adjudication=$(...)` and then `adjudicated=$?` on its own line. Under GitHub's `bash -e` an assignment whose right-hand side is a bare command substitution carries that substitution's status, so a non-zero adjudicator killed the step AT `adjudicated=$?` -- before the `printf`, before the `case`, before every line that reports a verdict. The branch that exists to report a blocking finding and the branch that reports an adjudicator which failed to START were therefore both dead code, on a REQUIRED check, producing no output at all; an uninstallable adjudicator was worse still, carrying its own 127 out of the job past the mapped exit codes. It seeds `adjudicated=0` and uses `|| adjudicated=$?`, and the seed is not redundant: on the success path the `||` branch never runs, so without it a clean adjudication reads as an empty string rather than as 0.

#1121 landed #675 -- the verdict step's refusal bound to its exit constant, so there is one site to mutate and a case can prove the refusal is what it observed. Test-only, and worth saying so rather than leaving it to be inferred: it never touched the generated workflow. A change whose title names a workflow and whose diff edits none is exactly the kind a reader credits with more than it did.

#1122 landed half of #1117. A #875 red now says WHICH of two conditions produced it: a transport failure that could not TAKE the reading, against a content divergence where the reading was taken and disagreed. Before, the two were indistinguishable in a shard of thousands of lines -- and they are opposite facts, because the first is UNMEASURED and only the second is a finding. #1117 stays OPEN for its other half.

#1125 landed #545: a refusal contract for failure intake, decided BEFORE the next scanner is added rather than after it has already landed green. A source whose precondition is unmet reports UNMEASURED naming itself and the missing input, and the aggregate is MEASURED only if every registered source was -- so a source that silently contributed nothing can no longer read as a source that found nothing. `AC-barren` is the part that makes it hold: it makes a cheaply-added fourth scanner impossible to land green, which is the direction this repo keeps having to re-learn.

#1107 landed #1078 -- #668's unscannable list has one shape, so the reporter reports it instead of crashing its consumer. Crash and clean reading are not the two options; the third is a reading that says what it could not read, which is the only one a caller can act on.

#1108 landed #1096, and the fact generalises past this repo: Bun does not propagate a late `process.env` write to a child spawned with no explicit `env`. So a test that poisons the environment AFTER start and then spawns is measuring nothing -- the child sees the environment as it was, the case passes, and the poisoning the case is NAMED for never reached anything. Poison at start or pass `env` explicitly; the third option is a green case over an experiment that did not happen.

#1109 landed #1104 and #1106 landed #1086 -- the same subject from two sides. `classify_path` redacted an unquotable scratch path by TRUNCATING it, so the record named a different path from the one it was about; a redaction that moves the referent is worse than none, because the record still reads as a record. It escapes now. And every directory a workflow prompt interpolates into a shell is quoted, which is the mechanical form of the same rule: quote the generator-controlled ones too, rather than asking every future editor to redo the reachability analysis correctly.

The session's theme is none of the eight. An npm partial outage reddened most of the fleet for about ninety minutes, and clearing it revealed THREE real failures it had been masking -- so the outage was not only a delay, it was a MASK, and the lost time was the smaller half of its cost. The control lesson is the sharper one: the status page still read `identified` while runners were already green, so neither the status page nor a local `curl` was the instrument. A re-run of a failed job was. A dependency's own status page is a claim about the dependency; it is not a reading of your runner.

What this entry is honest about, because the file it lives in exists to stop exactly this: eight PRs landed on `main` and nobody wrote a session entry, so `test/project-state-currency.test.ts` went red on `main` at 04:00Z and every open PR inherited it. The test is right, and it was not touched -- its sibling case exists precisely to catch someone neutralising it. The entry is also narrower than the night, and that is stated rather than implied: 141 PRs landed on the 2026-10-21 calendar day and session 56 narrated three of them, so this file is a narrative of what the DA merged and read, not a changelog of the fleet. #1128 (#713) is deliberately NOT in the list above although it merged at 04:21Z -- its base was `feat/713-migrate-product-hooks` and not `main`, so it has not landed here, and recording it as a merge would have been the same class of untruth this entry is repairing.
